openings.claim: Does Z1 depend on volunteers ticking a correct count, when O2 does not establish whether omissions begin during picking or filling? A tick alone cannot establish completeness for participants.
openings.delta: Expose the dependency between picked quantities, insertion ticks and actual contents; this is a diagnostic question, without a replacement assembly mechanism.
openings.prediction: If volunteers pick an incorrect quantity and then tick its insertion, apparently completed marks can coexist with missing items.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is loss during filling after correct picking. It predicts correct picked sets followed by incomplete envelopes, making insertion cues relevant.
openings.defeat: Observed correct picked sets with omissions arising exclusively during filling would defeat the upstream-count concern; consistently accurate marked envelopes would weaken the tick-reliability concern.
openings.probe: Observe four required marked kits with the same two volunteers, recording picked quantities, ticks and audited contents against the samples. Include observation and correction time in the 90-minute budget. This bounded diagnostic establishes neither improvement nor full-run success.
assumptions: Process-stage quantities can be recorded without materially changing behaviour or threatening completion; unverified.

openings.claim: Can A1 sustain local staging and replenishment on the existing table within the total time budget? O4 covers twelve kits; O5 reveals a later supply interruption despite available stock.
openings.delta: Question the scale and replenishment dependency behind the bounded-probe fit verdict, without redesigning staging.
openings.prediction: If replenishment introduces crowding or substantial handling time, the small-batch advantage will not establish 60 complete, correctly assigned kits within 90 minutes.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is a brief oversight in finding existing stock. It predicts negligible replenishment overhead and a workable footprint throughout assembly.
openings.defeat: A complete run using exactly two volunteers, existing supplies and the table, including replenishment and checking, meeting 90 minutes and at most one distribution correction would defeat this feasibility concern.
openings.probe: During the proposed required-kit batches, record occupied table space and elapsed replenishment/checking time, including opening existing packets. Stop if constraints are threatened. The observation may fit; eventual intervention feasibility remains unproven.
assumptions: Opened-packet footprint and replenishment overhead are unknown; existing stock is stipulated, sufficient staged capacity is not.

critiques.issue: Insertion ticks depend on accurate picked counts and faithful marking; the synthetic audit does not locate the omission stage.
A stoppable small probe does not verify full-run table and replenishment feasibility or achievement for participants and assemblers.
